title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 155
paragraphs: Croesus proposed this because he thought it was better for the Lydians than being sold into slavery. He knew that without a strong argument, he could not change Cyrus' mind. He also feared that even if the Lydians escaped this time, they might revolt again and be destroyed. Cyrus was pleased with the advice. He calmed his anger and said he would follow Croesus' suggestion. He summoned a Mede named Mazares and ordered him to tell the Lydians exactly what Croesus had recommended. He also ordered Mazares to sell into slavery everyone who had joined the Lydians in besieging Sardis—and above all, to bring Pactyas back alive.
